A woman behind a desk asked for his name and he gave it, and she typed it, and he watched her type it wrong in the same place the letter had. He said nothing. It was beginning to feel like a fact about him rather than a mistake, the way some people are tall.

He was told to sit. The chairs were the plastic kind that are bolted to a rail, six of them in a row, and he took the one at the end so that the empty ones would be beside him and not behind. On the wall there was a clock with no second hand. He found he missed it.
